$comment: Shared Go/TypeScript case table for the two StatusCounts roll-up helpers: AddCounts/addCounts (a bucket-wise sum of count sets) and SeverityTotals/severityTotals (the severity-only projection of one count set, whose `total` is the grand total across every status). Read by go/rollup_counts_test.go and test/status-counts-rollup.test.ts, so the two implementations cannot drift. Count sets are written in the TypeScript field spelling (noImpact); the Go test maps the table onto its own json tags. Omitted numbers are zero, so a case shows only the buckets it exercises. `inputs` is the argument list, `want` the summed count set, `wantSeverityTotals` the severity projection of `want`.

cases.name: no inputs sum to an empty count set
cases.note: the report asks for a sum before it knows whether a source has any baselines at all

cases.name: one count set sums to itself
two count sets add severity by severity inside each status bucket
three count sets roll up in one call
cases.note: the baselines then sources then whole shape the HTML report rolls up in

cases.name: a status bucket never bleeds into another
severity totals span every status, not only the failures
each bucket's total is added, never recomputed from its severities
cases.note: a count set whose total disagrees with its severities is not one the engine produces; the case pins that the helpers sum what they are given and invent no number, so a future implementation that derives total from the severity fields fails here instead of silently restating its inputs
